relevance_reason: This is the founding report of the disorder. It describes 5 patients from a consanguineous Slovakian Roma family with a biallelic SEL1L C141Y variant, and includes functional studies of the variant.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) named a disorder ENDI-agammaglobulinemia (ENDI-A) syndrome. It combines an ERAD-associated neurodevelopmental disorder with onset in infancy (ENDI) with infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia and no mature B cells, leading to frequent infections and early death.
quotes: These patients presented with not only ERAD-associated neurodevelopmental disorders with onset in infancy (ENDI) syndromes, but infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia with no mature B cells, resulting in frequent infections and early death.
This study reports a disease entity termed ENDI-agammaglobulinemia (ENDI-A) syndrome

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) reported 5 sibs from 2 consanguineous sibships within a large Roma family from an isolated region of southern Slovakia. All had problems with feeding from birth, with repeated vomiting after eating, failure to gain weight, pallor and gradual cachexia. They also had similar facial dysmorphisms (triangular face, big ears), severe axial hypotonia, global developmental delay, short stature, microcephaly, intellectual disability, and no speech. Three patients could not sit up or hold their heads up, and only patient 4 could sit without support, at age 4.5 years.
quotes: All patients started to have problems with food intake soon after birth, as they repeatedly vomited after eating (Table 1 and Supplemental Table 2). They were unable to gain weight, had pale skin color, gradually developed cachexia, and had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly (Table 1).
All patients exhibited intellectual disability and were unable to speak words and sentences

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) found that the patients had recurrent severe respiratory infections almost every month, including otitis media, sinusitis, bronchitis and pneumonia, often with respiratory insufficiency caused by food aspiration. Patients 3 and 4 were diagnosed with hearing impairment at 1 year of age, which the authors thought was likely secondary to otitis media. Patients 3, 4 and 5 had no detectable mature CD19+ memory B cells and no circulating immunoglobulins from 12 months of age. Their absolute CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts were largely normal, but the CD4:CD8 ratio was reduced.
quotes: these patients were frequently admitted to the hospital due to recurrent severe lower respiratory infection almost every month, starting from otitis media, sinusitis (bilateral maxillary and ethmoidal), to bronchitis and pneumonia

Immunological tests were performed with peripheral blood from patients 3, 4, and 5, which revealed no detectable mature CD19+ memory B cells in the circulation or circulating Igs at the age of 12 months and beyond (Table 2).
Although the absolute numbers of CD4+ helper and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells were largely in the normal ranges, the ratio of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells was reduced (Table 2)

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) found that a duodenal biopsy from patient 3 showed subtotal villous atrophy (Marsh IIIb enteropathy) with no CD20+ B cells. Patient 4 had COVID-19 with respiratory failure at 7.7 years. The course was prolonged, and no antigen-specific memory T-cell response was detected. All patients died young of infection, sepsis or respiratory failure: patient 1 at 2.9 years, patient 2 at 2 months, and patient 5 at 5.1 years.
quotes: A gut biopsy of patient 3 showed subtotal villous atrophy of the duodenum as Marsh IIIb enteropathy with no CD20+ B cells

Indeed, no specific cellular response measured by COVID antigen–specific memory T cells was detected in peripheral blood (Supplemental Figure 3B), indicative of defects in COVID antigen–induced T cell activation.
She died due to multiorgan failure at the age of 2.9 years.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) described further individual findings. Patient 1 developed marasmus and had acute renal failure and pulmonary hypertension. Patient 3 had a ventricular septal defect and epilepsy, with normal myelination on MRI. Patient 4 had leukoencephalopathy on MRI, ptosis, partial papillary atrophy and sideropenic anemia. Patient 5 had leukoencephalopathy, later discrete cortical atrophy, ptosis, micropenis, central hypothyroidism, hypoplastic thymus, hepatopathy and dystrophic nails.
quotes: She was treated because of acute renal failure and pulmonary hypertension.
Patient 3 (IV-3) was born with a ventricular septal defect.
Patient 4 (IV-5) did brain MRI at the age of 10 months, showing unspecific leukoencephalopathy frontal and occipital bilaterally, but she had no seizures.
He had a micropenis, central hypothyroidism, hypoplastic thymus, hepatopathy, and dystrophic nails.

findings.statement: In 5 affected sibs from 2 consanguineous sibships of a Slovakian Roma family with ENDI-A, Weis et al. (2024) identified a homozygous c.422G>A transition in exon 4 of the SEL1L gene (NM_005065.6), resulting in a cys141-to-tyr (C141Y) substitution. The variant was found by whole-exome sequencing of 2 patients and their parents, assuming recessive inheritance, and was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It was found in all 5 patients but not in parents or unaffected sibs. It affects a conserved cysteine in the luminal fibronectin type II domain that forms a disulfide bond with Cys168. The authors classified the variant as pathogenic under ACMG criteria but acknowledged that causality could not be firmly established without a knockin mouse.
quotes: Two variants were identified in individual patients, SEL1L p.Cys141Tyr (NM_005065.6: exon 4: c.422G>A) and fatty acyl-CoA reductase 2 (FAR2) p.Arg490Trp
Moreover, Sanger sequencing further confirmed the biallelic SEL1LC141Y variant in all 5 patients, but not in parents or unaffected siblings (Figure 1, C and D).
From combining evidence from genetics and in silico and in vitro analysis, SEL1LC141Y has been considered to be a pathogenic variant with a total score of 14 points based on ACMG criteria.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) found that a FAR2 variant, R490W, also identified by exome sequencing, did not segregate with disease (in patient 2) and was excluded as causal. Chromosome analysis, SNP array and next-generation sequencing found no other genomic imbalance or variant to explain the phenotypes. aCGH found no large deletions or duplications.
quotes: As Sanger sequencing confirmed the segregation of the FAR2 variant with symptoms in patient 2 (Supplemental Figure 2) and as loss of FAR2 function is not linked to neurological disorder or agammaglobulinemia, we excluded it from being causal for these patients.

Other variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders or hypogammaglobulinemia were examined independently with chromosome analysis, SNParray, and next-generation sequencing (NGS); however, these tests did not show any other genomic imbalances or other associated genetic variants.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) reported a female sib (IV-4) who carried 1 C141Y allele. She was born with alobar holoprosencephaly, cleft lip and palate, 'frog' eyes, low-set ears, microcephaly, pterygium colli, polydactyly/syndactyly, anal malformation, contractures, and atrioventricular septal defect with patent ductus arteriosus. She died at 9 days of age of cardiorespiratory failure and had no immune problems.
quotes: Of note, the IV-4 individual, carrying 1 allele SEL1LC141Y, was born with multiple malformations (alobar holoprosencephaly, “frog” eyes, anus malformation, congenital heart defects, etc.) and died from cardiorespiratory failure at 9 days of age (Figure 1A).
The patient had no infection or problem with immunity as in the other siblings with agammaglobulinemia.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) treated patients 3, 4 and 5 with IgG replacement every 4 weeks. Acute infections improved substantially, but chronic respiratory symptoms continued to recur. All 3 eventually deteriorated suddenly with sepsis and multiorgan failure.
quotes: Consequently, IgG was given as a replacement therapy every 4 weeks in these patients. Indeed, after replacement therapy was initiated, a substantial improvement in acute infections was noted.
However, all 3 were observed to have a sudden dramatic deterioration of the clinical condition due to sepsis with multiorgan failure.

findings.statement: In patient fibroblasts, Weis et al. (2024) found that SEL1L protein was largely undetectable and HRD1 protein was reduced by more than 90%, with normal mRNA levels. Both proteins were unstable, and the ERAD substrates IRE1-alpha and CD147 accumulated. The lectins OS9 and ERLEC1 were decreased. There was no overt unfolded protein response, but ER chaperones were elevated. Biopsies from patients' duodenum also showed reduced SEL1L and HRD1.
quotes: Strikingly, SEL1L protein levels were significantly reduced and largely undetectable in the patient fibroblasts compared with in WT cells (Figure 3, A and B).
HRD1 protein levels were also significantly reduced, by over 90%, in patient cells
Hence, we conclude that SEL1LC141Y causes severe ERAD dysfunction, but is not associated with an overt UPR.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) compared knockin HEK293T cells carrying C141Y with cells carrying the hypomorphic ENDI variants SEL1L M528R, SEL1L G585D and HRD1 P398L. C141Y cells had the lowest SEL1L and HRD1 levels and the highest substrate accumulation, indicating the most severe ERAD dysfunction. Effects were milder than in SEL1L-null cells, suggesting that C141Y is not a complete loss of function. The authors proposed an inverse correlation between ERAD function and disease severity.
quotes: Hence, we conclude that SEL1LC141Y-expressing cells exhibit the most severe ERAD dysfunction among all the hypomorphic variants.
suggesting that SEL1LC141Y is not a complete loss-of-function variant, which may explain why the patients could survive for months or even years

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) found that the C141Y variant did not impair formation of the ERAD complex. Disrupting the other FNII disulfide bond (C127Y) had similar effects, whereas deleting the whole FNII domain left ERAD function largely normal. Proteasome inhibition, or deletion of HRD1 but not RNF5, rescued SEL1L levels, and the accumulated mutant SEL1L formed high-molecular-weight aggregates. The authors concluded that the unpaired cysteine causes HRD1-mediated, proteasome-dependent self-destruction of the SEL1L-HRD1 complex.
quotes: Strikingly, deletion of HRD1, but not RNF5, significantly rescued the protein levels and stability of SEL1L in SEL1LC127Y and SEL1LC141Y KI HEK293T cells (Figure 7, B, C, E, and F).
Hence, we conclude that the FNII domain of SEL1L is dispensable for SEL1L-HRD1 ERAD function and that the SEL1LC141Y variant affects ERAD complex stability, likely through the unpaired Cys.
In conclusion, SEL1LC141Y causes proteasome-mediated self-destruction of the SEL1L-HRD1 ERAD complex.

findings.statement: Weis et al. (2024) noted that, unlike ENDI patients with hypomorphic SEL1L (G585D, M528R) or HRD1 (P398L) variants who survived into their teens and twenties, patients with the more severe C141Y variant had B-cell immunodeficiency and died early. The authors attributed this to differing degrees of ERAD dysfunction.
quotes: These differences likely reflect different degrees of ERAD dysfunction among these variants; while SEL1L (p.Gly585Asp, p.Met528Arg) and HRD1 (p.Pro398Leu) variants are hypomorphic with moderate ERAD dysfunction, the SEL1L p.Cys141Tyr variant is much more severe

relevance_reason: The paper reports no patients or human variants, but it characterizes the function of the Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD complex in B cell development using mouse models, showing that B cell-specific Sel1L deficiency blocks development at the large-to-small pre-B cell transition and markedly reduces peripheral B cells. This is mechanistic/animal-model evidence a curator would cite for the agammaglobulinemia component of the entry.

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) generated B cell-specific Sel1L-deficient mice (Sel1L-CD19) by crossing Sel1L flox/flox mice on the C57BL/6 background with CD19-Cre mice; the mutant mice were born in a normal Mendelian ratio and appeared healthy with no obvious growth defects, but spleen weights were significantly reduced, the percentage of peripheral B cells in spleen, blood, and lymph nodes was reduced by 60-75%, and absolute numbers of splenic B cells were more than 75% lower than in controls, whereas CD4+, CD8+ T and myeloid cells were not affected. The authors concluded that Sel1L is required for B cell development.
quotes: The Sel1LCD19 mice and their control Sel1Lf/f littermates were born in a normal Mendelian ratio (not shown) and appeared healthy with no obvious growth defects (Fig. 1B).

The percentage of peripheral B cells in spleen, blood, and lymph nodes was reduced by 60-75% (Fig. 1E) and the absolute numbers of splenic B cells were >75% lower in Sel1LCD19 mice compared to controls, while other cell types, including CD4+, CD8+ T and myeloid cells were not affected (Fig. 1F-G and Fig. S1C).
Hence, we concluded that Sel1L is required for B cell development.

phenotypes.text: normal T cell and myeloid cell numbers

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) found that Sel1L-CD19 mice had a severe developmental block at the transition from large to small pre-B cells: recirculating mature (B220high IgM+) and immature (B220low IgM+) bone marrow B cells were significantly decreased, pro-B cells were slightly elevated, SLC+ CD2- pre-B I and large pre-B cells were twice as numerous, and SLC- CD2+ small pre-B cells were reduced by 50%; apoptotic rates were comparable between cohorts, and neither Sel1L heterozygosity nor CD19-Cre expression alone affected B cell development.
quotes: Within the pro-/pre-B cell compartment of the BM, SLC+ CD2− pre-B I and large pre-B (II) cells were twice as many, whereas SLC− CD2+ small pre-B cells were reduced by 50% in the Sel1LCD19 mice compared to Sel1Lf/f littermates (Fig. 2C and Fig. S2B).
Thus, B cell-specific Sel1L deficiency results in a severe developmental defect at the transition from the large to small pre-B cells.

Both Sel1L heterozygosity and CD19-Cre expression as in Sel1Lf/+;CD19-Cre (Sel1LCD19/+) mice had no effect on B cell development (Fig. S2D), splenic B cell composition (Fig. S2E) and spleen weight (Fig. S2F).

phenotypes.text: block in B cell development at large to small pre-B cell transition
decreased immature and mature bone marrow B cells
increased apoptosis of B cell precursors

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) showed that the B cell developmental block in Sel1L-CD19 mice was Chop-independent: although BiP and Chop were moderately elevated in large pre-B cells of mutant mice, Chop deficiency in Sel1L-CD19;Chop-/- mice had no impact on the low spleen weight, the paucity of peripheral B cells, or the developmental block at the large pre-B cell stage.
quotes: Indeed, a subset of ER stress-responsive genes such as BiP and Chop were moderately elevated in the large pre-B cells of Sel1LCD19 mice (Fig. S3A).

However, Chop deficiency had no impact on the B cell developmental defects associated with the loss of Sel1L, in terms of low spleen weight (Fig. S3B), paucity of the B cell compartment within the peripheral lymphocyte pool (Fig. S3C), and the developmental block at the large pre-B cell stage in the BM (Fig. S3D-G).

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) reported that expression of the Sel1L and Hrd1 genes was induced around the pre-B cell stage in developing lymphocytes, preceding that of the ER chaperones BiP and Edem1, suggesting a role for Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD in early lymphopoiesis.
quotes: Expression of Sel1L and Hrd1 genes was induced around the pre-B cell stage in developing lymphocytes, preceding that of ER chaperones BiP and Edem1 (Fig. 1A), suggesting a possible role of Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD in early lymphopoiesis.

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) identified the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) complex, rather than its individual components, as an endogenous substrate of the Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD complex: protein levels of the three pre-BCR components (Igmu, lambda5, VpreB) were dramatically increased and stabilized in pro-/pre-B cells of Sel1L-CD19 mice while transcript levels were unchanged, and loss of either Sel1L or Hrd1 in 70z/3 pre-B cells raised steady-state pre-BCR levels and increased the Igmu half-life from about 60 min to over 120 min with dramatically reduced Igmu ubiquitination.
quotes: While total levels (intracellular and surface) of c-Kit and IL-7Rα protein were comparable, protein levels of three main components of the pre-BCR complex were dramatically increased in the pro-/pre-B cells of Sel1LCD19 mice (Fig. 3B).

Loss of either Sel1L or Hrd1 in the 70z/3 cells increased steady-state protein levels of all three components of the pre-BCR complex (Fig. 4B-C), and led to Igμ protein stabilization, with its half-life increasing from approximately 60 min to over 120 min (Fig. 4D).

Furthermore, ubiquitination of Igμ protein was reduced dramatically in Sel1L−/− or Hrd1−/− 70z/3 cells (Fig. 4F and not shown), pointing to the indispensable role of Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD in pre-BCR ubiquitination and degradation.

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) showed that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD deficiency led to increased ER exit and elevated surface pre-BCR (nearly 3-fold more endoH-resistant Igmu), increased phosphorylation of the downstream effector Syk, and more than 50% more BrdU-positive cycling pro-/pre-B cells in the bone marrow of Sel1L-CD19 mice, with proliferation of lambda5+ large pre-B cells increased more than 2.5-fold; the authors concluded that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD is required to attenuate pre-BCR signaling by promoting its turnover, and that the mutant mice phenocopy models with gain-of-function pre-BCR signaling.
quotes: Sel1L deficiency resulted in a nearly 3-fold increase in endoH-resistant and peptide-N-glycosidase F (PNGase F)-sensitive Igμ protein, indicative of increased ER exit of the pre-BCR complex in the absence of Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD (Fig. 5D).
Furthermore, the total number of BrdU-positive cycling pro-/pre-B cells in BM was increased by more than 50% in Sel1LCD19 mice compared to Sel1Lf/f mice (Fig. 5H and Fig. S6D).
Instead, our data demonstrate that the Sel1LCD19 mice phenocopy those of mouse models with gain-of-function pre-BCR signaling.

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) found that the pre-BCR, but not the mature BCR, is a Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD substrate: in LPS-differentiated 70z/3 cells and in mature splenic B cells from inducible Sel1L-knockout (Sel1L-ERCre) mice, the steady-state level, stability, endoH sensitivity and surface IgM of Igmu in the BCR complex were unaffected by Sel1L deficiency, plasma cell differentiation and total IgG were likewise unaffected, and Igmu interacted with Sel1L and OS9 more extensively in pre-B than in mature B cells.
quotes: Unlike Igμ in the pre-BCR, neither the steady-state protein level or stability of Igμ in the BCR complex, nor its endoH sensitivity (i.e. ER exit), were affected by Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD deficiency in mature B cells (Fig. 6B-D).
Moreover, plasma cell differentiation, cell size and total IgG levels in LPS/IL-4-treated mature primary B cells (Sel1Lf/f and Sel1LERCre) were not affected by Sel1L deficiency (Fig. S7A-C).
Indeed, Igμ interacted with several components of the ERAD machinery, including Sel1L and OS9, to a greater extent in pre-B cells compared to mature B cells (Fig. 6H).

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) demonstrated that ERAD-mediated pre-BCR degradation required BiP but not the unique region of lambda5: depletion of BiP with subtilase cytotoxin SubAB reduced the Igmu-Sel1L interaction and stabilized Igmu protein, whereas a mutant lambda5 lacking the unique region (JC lambda5) did not alter steady-state pre-BCR levels or Igmu half-life and the JC lambda5-containing complex remained an ERAD substrate.
quotes: Depletion of BiP with the subtilase cytotoxin SubAB significantly reduced the interaction between Igμ and Sel1L (Fig. 7A) and stabilized Igμ protein (Fig. 7B).
Consistently, JC λ5 expression failed to affect Igμ protein half-life (Fig. 7F).
Hence, we concluded that BiP, but not the unique region of λ5, is required for the recognition of the pre-BCR complex as an ERAD substrate in pre-B cells.

findings.statement: Ji et al. (2016) noted that global Sel1L-deficient mice are embryonic lethal and that acute Sel1L deletion in adult mice results in pancreatic atrophy and premature lethality, with Sel1L deficiency in adipocytes causing intracellular retention of lipoprotein lipase and hypertriglyceridemia.
quotes: While Sel1L-deficient mice are embryonic lethal, acute Sel1L deletion in adult mice results in pancreatic atrophy and premature lethality. In adipocytes, Sel1L deficiency causes intracellular retention of lipoprotein lipase, leading to hypertriglyceridemia.
